name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is one of Europe's smallest EV markets: 763 electric vehicles were registered at the end of 2024, and Eurostat-based figures show 71 new battery-electric cars in 2025 (0.7% of new car registrations). Public charging is split between the utility Elektroprivreda BiH, private networks such as e-GO and single chargers at hotels, malls and fuel stations; most operators publish no prices, there is no official nationwide count and no Tesla Supercharger. Only a few firms publish home-charger prices (about 670–2,900 KM per wallbox), household electricity is regulated separately in the Federation, Republika Srpska and Brčko District, and the Federation's 2026 EV purchase subsidy (up to 12,000 KM) was fully reserved within two days.

home_companies.name: e-punionice.ba (Vektra d.o.o.)
home_companies.what: Online shop for EV charging equipment: wall-mounted home chargers (36 models in its wallbox category), mobile chargers, commercial and DC chargers, adapters. Its business page offers installation and connection of chargers to software for monitoring and billing ('praćenje i naplatu').
home_companies.price: Wallboxes 670–2,895 KM, e.g. dé Wallbox 11 kW 845–1,190 KM, Easee Charge Core 2,279 KM, Tesla Wall Connector 22 kW 2,195 KM; twin-socket Stekerr P1 units 8,549–9,159 KM. VAT not stated.
home_companies.installation_note: Business page: 'Profesionalna montaža traje svega nekoliko sati' (professional installation takes a few hours); the contact page offers help with charger installation ('ugradnju punionice'). Installation price not published.

subsidies.programme: Federation of BiH – Environmental Protection Fund (Fond za zaštitu okoliša FBiH), public call JP EV 2026 for new electric vehicles
subsidies.amount: Up to 12,000 KM for a battery-electric vehicle and up to 10,000 KM for a plug-in hybrid, at most 30% of the vehicle price (about €6,135.50 / €5,112.92); call budget 500,000 KM
subsidies.who: Adults resident in the Federation of BiH; legal entities and sole traders (obrti) registered in the Federation. New M1 (passenger) and N1 (light goods) vehicles only, never registered before.
subsidies.deadline: Until funds are used up, at the latest 31.12.2026. Temporarily closed on 18.09.2026 after all funds were reserved; it reopens only if money remains after the submitted applications are processed.
subsidies.note: Opened 16.09.2026; applications via e-prijava.fzofbih.org.ba, handled in order of arrival. Chargers are not mentioned as eligible. Closure notice: https://fzofbih.org.ba/2026/09/18/privremeno-zatvaranje-javnog-poziva-za-sufinanciranje-nabave-elektricnih-vozila-za-2026-godinu-zbog-rezervacije-raspolozivih-sredstava/ . Oslobođenje (15.01.2024) reported Federation incentives of 10,000 KM per vehicle in 2023.
subsidies.source_title: Fond za zaštitu okoliša FBiH – JP EV 2026, tekst poziva

buildings.topic: Work on common parts for an owner's own installation (Federation of BiH)
buildings.text: An owner may change their own unit, but if the change requires work on common parts of the building it is allowed only if it is usual or serves an important interest of the owner; otherwise any co-owner can forbid it. Co-owners cannot, however, forbid laying lines for light, gas, energy, water and telephone. The law does not mention EV chargers.
buildings.law: Zakon o stvarnim pravima FBiH (Službene novine FBiH 66/13, 100/13, 32/19), Art. 95

buildings.topic: Improvements to common parts (Federation of BiH)
buildings.text: Owners who together hold a majority of co-ownership shares can decide on improvements to the building without everyone's consent, provided the improvements do not harm the outvoted owners.
buildings.law: Zakon o stvarnim pravima FBiH, Art. 99

buildings.topic: Ordinary and extraordinary management (Federation of BiH)
buildings.text: A building in unit ownership is managed by the owners under the general co-ownership rules and they must keep a common reserve fund. Ordinary management needs owners holding more than half of the shares; works beyond ordinary management (for example change of use, leasing, larger repairs or alterations not needed for maintenance) need the consent of all co-owners.
buildings.law: Zakon o stvarnim pravima FBiH, Art. 31, 32 and 97

buildings.topic: Work on common parts for an owner's own installation (Republika Srpska)
buildings.text: Work on common parts is allowed only if the change is usual or serves an important interest, otherwise any co-owner can forbid it — except laying lines for light, gas, energy, water, telephone and similar devices needed by the state of technology. The law does not mention EV chargers.
buildings.law: Zakon o stvarnim pravima Republike Srpske (Službeni glasnik RS 124/08 … 21/26), Art. 95(1)(b)
buildings.source_title: Zakon o stvarnim pravima (Republika Srpska) – Paragraf.ba

buildings.text: Owners holding a majority of co-ownership shares can decide on improvements to common parts, provided the outvoted owners are not harmed. Ordinary management needs more than half of the shares; extraordinary management needs all co-owners.
buildings.law: Zakon o stvarnim pravima Republike Srpske, Art. 99(2), 31 and 32
buildings.source_title: Zakon o stvarnim pravima (Republika Srpska) – Paragraf.ba

buildings.text: No provider was found that markets a shared-garage charging service to apartment owners (handling co-owner consent, per-user metering and billing). The closest published offer is e-punionice.ba's business package: installation in a few hours and connection of the charger to software for monitoring and billing.

policy.text: At the third Green Agenda ministerial meeting for the Western Balkans (Žabljak, 18–19.09.2026), the Transport Community secretariat said it gives regional partners technical assistance on alignment with the EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), preparation of national policy frameworks and a regional roadmap, aiming at an interoperable charging and refuelling network along the TEN-T network.

In the Federation of BiH the energy regulator FERK keeps a register of EV charging service providers; it lists 2 providers (e-GO and Porsche Inter Auto BH) with 20 stations, all in Sarajevo, and its last entry is dated 02.04.2024. EPBiH's own network is not in the register.

gaps: The WebSearch budget ran out early in this pass; the rest was done by opening official pages and already-known URLs. Only 3 home-charger sellers could be verified and none in Banja Luka or Tuzla (the 22.09.2026 pass had the same gap).
Installation prices for home chargers: not published by any BiH source found.
Republika Srpska: no verified home-charger seller or installer. The OLX shop 'Elektropunjaci' (Bijeljina) has no active listings and was last online about four years ago.
Hager's BiH site (hager.com/ba) shows its witty charger range but names no sellers or prices. Schrack's e-mobility products do not display without JavaScript.

EPBiH public charging prices: announced for mojaenergija.epbih.ba/elektromobilnost/ but not published as of 23.09.2026. e-GO prices are not on its site. Whether EPBiH charging is still in a free test phase is not stated.

Republika Srpska: no public charging operator with published prices found; the ERS, Elektroprivreda HZ HB, Petrol BiH, INA BiH/Energopetrol and m:tel sites have no charging information. The operator behind 'easy2charge' was not identified.
No official nationwide count of public charge points. FERK's Federation register was last updated 02.04.2024; map and media figures range from 78 to about 500.
BIHAMK has not yet published its 2025 registered-vehicles report; no IDDEEA or statistics-agency series by fuel type was found.
EPBiH household tariff tables are published as images; EPBiH figures come from media, and whether they include network charges is not confirmed.
Brčko District: no EV purchase or charger subsidy found.
No subsidy for home chargers found in either entity; the Federation's JP EV 2026 does not list chargers as eligible.

Apartment buildings: no EV-specific rule in the entity property laws; the Federation's cantonal building-management laws (e.g. Sarajevo Canton) could not be opened; no rules found on metering or billing a charger in a shared garage.
Policy: no BiH national policy framework for alternative fuels or NECP e-mobility target was verified; the Energy Community's BiH page has no e-mobility content.
Tuzla Canton charging-station co-financing: only the 2025 budget line is reported; no 2026 call found.

Blocked or not loading: autoklub.net (robots.txt timeout), portal.sef.ba (timeout), energologija.com (timeout), ekapija.com (403), ferk.ba tariff pages (robots.txt fetch failed), chargerbh.ba (domain does not resolve), akta.ba article on the Hager charger in Zenica (server error), otisak.ba (did not resolve), paragraf.ba index of Republika Srpska laws (disallowed by robots.txt).
